title: Transparent fallback and SLO preservation during Hosted API 5xx waves
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Several enterprise customers have escalated after intermittent 5xx waves and timeouts on the Hosted API resulted in large end-to-end latency increases and amplified client retries. This ticket implements a transparent fallback and SLO-preservation strategy that routes traffic to compatible lightweight model variants or an async degradation path while preserving customer-visible SLA guarantees and minimizing error amplification.

Background: During recent incidents we observed that upstream GPU pools momentarily saturated or hit a slowpath that produced long tail latencies and 5xx responses. Client SDKs retried aggressively and fanouted requests, amplifying the pressure. Previous mitigations reduced harm but caused visible request drops or forced manual tenant quarantines. We need an automated, predictable mechanism that: preserves per-tenant p95 latency SLOs, avoids large-scale 5xx waves, and provides clear customer communications and canary rollouts.

Proposal: Implement a multi-tier fallback controller with the following components: (1) a tenant-scoped admission controller that enforces dynamic concurrency caps and backs off retries by injecting Retry-After headers for eligible clients; (2) a transparent model-fallback capability that switches requests from a primary GPU-accelerated model to a verified CPU/quantized cheaper variant or smaller model family when backend error rate/latency crosses thresholds; (3) an async-degrade queue: when both compute and fallback capacity are constrained, accept the request and return an immediate 202 with a polling handle (or webhook) and best-effort execution; (4) an emergency fastpath for high-priority customers that routes to reserved capacity where available.

Key trade-offs: The fallback path will change generation quality for some prompts — we will restrict transparent fallback to model families where we have validated prompt-level quality baselines; for requests requiring strict model fidelity customers can opt out via tenant flags (and be routed to reserved capacity or best-effort). Async-degrade reduces perceived errors but increases complexity in observable billing and customer UX (polling/webhooks). The admission controller is conservative to avoid unnecessary degradation.

Outcomes: Reduced 5xx rate and p95 SLO violations during backend saturation, fewer customer escalations, a documented customer opt-out path, and an operator-visible dashboard for fallback events and quality regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Admission controller enforces a per-tenant concurrency cap with adjustable hysteresis and publishes cap metrics to the console.
Model-fallback implemented for at least two high-traffic model families with automated verification that fallback model meets quality thresholds for provided prompt suites.
Requests can transparently return 202 + polling handle for async-degrade path and complete successfully within documented SLAs (e.g., 2 minutes for non-streaming inference).
SDK/HTTP clients receive clear Retry-After or 202 responses; SDKs updated to honor Retry-After and expose polling helper (PR in SDK repo).
Dashboard tiles display fallback events, counts by tenant, p95/p99 pre- and post-fallback latencies, and error rates; alerts fire on large-scale fallbacks.
Canary rollout plan executed with traffic-shaping and anomaly detection; rollback path validated during canary.
implementation_notes: Admission controller: implement token-bucket per tenant in frontdoor proxy (edge) and a control-plane config endpoint to set caps per plan tier.
Fallback model registry: add metadata flags on model catalog entries to mark 'compatible_fallbacks' and validation artifacts (prompt sets + baseline scores).
Async queue: new service 'degrade-queue' (stateless API + durable task store) with idempotency keys; expose polling handle format and webhook contract.
SDK changes: add honorRetryAfter() helper and a pollAsyncResult() convenience method. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/4120
Operator controls: feature flag gate 'transparent_fallback_v1' with per-tenant override in console (console PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/1286).
Testing: end-to-end load tests against canary clusters emulating the recent incident pattern; create synthetic prompt sets for fallback quality validation and add to nightly regression suite.
Telemetry: emit 'fallback_decision' events with reasons (latency_threshold, error_rate, cap_reached), and include model_version, tenant_id, request_id. Hook into existing cost-accounting pipeline.

Docs & comms: Draft customer-facing KB explaining degradation modes and opt-out, update SLAs to reflect transparent fallback behavior for non-pinned models. Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFERENCE/Transparent+Fallback+Design

2025-02-24 Emma Kline (SRE): Suggest we add circuit-breaker metric 'consecutive_backend_timeouts' to avoid oscillation. Also recommended a 30s soft-delay before switching to CPU fallback to prevent flapping. Added to implementation notes.

2025-02-26 Product review (Liam Ortiz): Customer opt-out UX required; adding 'model_pin' account flag and docs. Also requested a list of customers eligible for the emergency fastpath and billing implications.

2025-02-28 QA (Priya Nair): Integration test plan reviewed. Added tests for idempotency keys and webhook delivery guarantees. Noted possible race on request cancellation during async-degrade. Assign to Diego to triage.
